page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-8-lssd is an x86_64 instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance includes 62 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a 504 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. Storage is directly attached via a integrated 402 GB NVMe local SSD, while GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong execution in specific integer and text manipulation tasks. Single-threaded gzip compression scored in the top 25% at 35.4 GB/sec, and Geekbench text processing achieved a top-tier placement at 2924.0. CPU performance measured by stress-ng and Geekbench (1899.0 single-core, 7155.0 multi-core) remains within the median tier. In inference evaluations, small language model text generation achieved a strong 283.92 tokens per second. Conversely, memory subsystem results show constraints under heavy data access: uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 39.24 GB/sec and the PassMark memory benchmark placed in the lower 25th percentile.

The inclusion of dedicated local NVMe storage combined with high memory capacity provides efficient resource density for input/output intensive jobs without incurring auxiliary network storage fees. However, the throughput limits on uncached memory access represent an architectural tradeoff for large-footprint tasks. The instance is suited for in-memory databases such as Redis, local scratch caching, text analysis pipelines, compression tasks, and general data processing requiring local high-speed disk persistence.
